goals.name: Growth hormone
goals.label: Growth hormone
goals.title: Growth hormone peptides: what is approved | Peptide Chooser
goals.h1: Growth hormone peptides, compared with the approved medicines.
goals.description: Sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295, tesamorelin and IGF-1 LR3: what each is, which is FDA approved and for what, and what clinics and shops charge.
goals.short_answer: Growth hormone itself (somatropin) is FDA approved, mainly for children and adults with growth hormone deficiency. Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is approved only to reduce belly fat in adults with HIV and lipodystrophy. Sermorelin's approved product left the market years ago; online clinics prescribe pharmacy-made versions. CJC-1295, ipamorelin and IGF-1 LR3 are research-use products with no approved version; we show their prices and checks and do not link to the shops.
goals.intro: Growth hormone itself is FDA approved for growth hormone deficiency. The peptides sold to raise it are pharmacy-made or research-use, and none is approved for that.

peptides.name: Growth hormone (somatropin)
peptides.plain: Lab-made human growth hormone, a shot on prescription. FDA approved mainly for growth hormone deficiency.
peptides.does: Approved for children who do not grow because of growth hormone deficiency or some other conditions, and for adults with growth hormone deficiency. Not approved for healthy adults who want more muscle or energy.
peptides.status_plain: FDA approved, mainly for growth hormone deficiency.

peptides.name: Tesamorelin (Egrifta)
peptides.plain: A daily shot on prescription, approved only to reduce belly fat in people with HIV, not for muscle.
peptides.does: A daily shot approved only to reduce belly fat in people with HIV. Sold off-label by clinics for "growth hormone".
peptides.status_plain: FDA approved for HIV-related belly fat only.
peptides.top_pick_why: Approved only for HIV-related belly fat, not for raising growth hormone (owner, 31 Oct 2026, on /muscle/).
peptides.no_link: Approved for HIV belly fat only
peptides.line_one: daily shot for belly fat in HIV

peptides.name: CJC-1295
peptides.plain: A peptide meant to make the body release growth hormone, in research-use vials. Not approved.
peptides.does: A long-acting copy of the hormone that tells the body to release growth hormone. In two trials in healthy adults it raised growth hormone and IGF-I; the trials did not measure muscle or strength.
peptides.line_one: vials sold to raise growth hormone

peptides.name: Ipamorelin
peptides.plain: A peptide meant to make the body release growth hormone, in research-use vials. Not approved.
peptides.does: Acts on a different receptor than CJC-1295, with the same aim. Its one larger trial in people, 117 patients after bowel surgery, found it did no better than a placebo. The FDA lists safety concerns for it.
peptides.line_one: vials sold to raise growth hormone

peptides.name: IGF-1 LR3
peptides.plain: Sold as a form of IGF-1, in research-use vials. Drugs@FDA lists no product with it.
peptides.does: Sold for growth by research-use shops. The approved IGF-1 medicine is a different product, mecasermin (Increlex).

peptides.name: Sermorelin
peptides.plain: A pharmacy-mixed shot on prescription that makes the body release growth hormone. No approved product.
peptides.status: No FDA-approved product on the market
peptides.does: A growth-hormone-releasing shot from compounding pharmacies; the approved brand was taken off the market years ago.
peptides.status_plain: No FDA-approved product on the market.

goals.for: For raising growth hormone: what is approved and for whom, and what the sold peptides are.

goals.name: Sleep
goals.label: Sleep
goals.title: Peptides for sleep: DSIP and the evidence | Peptide Chooser
goals.h1: Peptides for sleep, compared with the evidence.
goals.description: DSIP is the peptide sold for sleep. It is not FDA approved, and its trials in people are small and old. What it is, its status, and what shops charge.
goals.short_answer: DSIP (delta sleep-inducing peptide) is the peptide sold for sleep; it is not FDA approved, and its trials in people are small and from the 1980s. Its nomination for pharmacy compounding was withdrawn, and the FDA says it lacks the safety information to know whether it would cause harm.
goals.intro: DSIP, the peptide sold for sleep, is not FDA approved, and its trials in people are small and old.

peptides.name: DSIP
peptides.plain: Delta sleep-inducing peptide, sold for sleep in research-use vials. Not approved; small, old trials in people.
peptides.does: In a 1987 study, 14 adults with chronic insomnia slept better on 7 nights of DSIP shots than on placebo nights; we found no larger or newer trial. The FDA says it lacks the safety information to know whether it would cause harm.

goals.for: For trouble sleeping: what the peptide sold for it is, and what its trials in people showed.

goals.name: Energy
goals.label: Energy
goals.title: Peptides for energy: MOTS-c and NAD+ | Peptide Chooser
goals.h1: Peptides for energy: what is sold, and what the evidence shows.
goals.description: MOTS-c, NAD+ and sermorelin are sold for energy. None is FDA approved for it. What each one is, the evidence in people, and what clinics and shops charge.
goals.short_answer: No peptide is FDA approved for energy. MOTS-c has been tested in animals only; since 30 Oct 2026 an HHS policy lets licensed pharmacies compound it under conditions, which is not FDA approval. NAD+ is not a peptide at all; clinics sell it as shots and drips without approval. Sermorelin's approved product left the market years ago; online clinics prescribe pharmacy-made versions.
goals.intro: No peptide is approved for energy. MOTS-c is tested in animals only, NAD+ is not a peptide, and sermorelin has no approved product on the market.

peptides.name: MOTS-c
peptides.plain: A peptide sold for energy, in vials labelled for lab use. Not approved and tested in animals only.

peptides.status: Not a peptide; compounded, not FDA approved
peptides.does: Not a peptide: a vitamin-B3-derived molecule sold by clinics as shots or drips for energy.
peptides.line_one: clinic shots or drips, not a peptide
